property_summary: Calling lockInGuess reverts if and only if the sent msg.value is not exactly 1 ether.

Calling lockInGuess with any amount of Ether either always succeeds (does not revert) when that amount equals 1 ether, and always reverts when it does not; therefore for original C, reverted == (amount != 1 ether).

For contract C, calling lockInGuess with any caller and any bytes32 should only revert when msg.value is not exactly 1 ether (i.e., sending 1 ether must never cause revert), so sending 1 ether always succeeds.
For any caller and any hash, calling lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether must not revert (reverted == false whenever amount == 1 ether).

For any caller who successfully calls lockInGuess with 1 ether, the reference contract records a nonzero future block number for that caller (guesses[msg.sender].block != 0); the mutant that omits setting the block leaves it at 0 and thus violates this property for such calls.

For any caller who successfully calls lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether, the reference contract records a nonzero stored block number for that caller (guesses[caller].block != 0); the mutant that omits setting the block leaves it zero and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

After any externally successful lockInGuess call (caller sends 1 ether), the reference contract records a nonzero stored block number for that caller (guesses[caller].block != 0); the mutant that omits setting the block leaves it zero, so there exist inputs (a caller sending 1 ether) that make the mutant violate this rule.

For any caller who sends exactly 1 ether when calling lockInGuess, the correct contract records a nonzero stored block number (so a subsequent getter reflecting that block is > 0), whereas the mutant that omits setting the block leaves it zero and thus violates this rule for such inputs.

For any caller who successfully calls lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether, the reference contract records a nonzero stored block number for that caller (guesses[caller].block != 0); the mutant that omits assigning that block leaves it zero, so there exist inputs (a caller sending 1 ether and a guess) that make the mutant violate this property.

For any caller who successfully calls lockInGuess with 1 ether when they had no prior guess, the stored guesses(caller).block is strictly greater than the block number at which lockInGuess was executed (reference sets block = current + 1); the mutant sets it equal to the current block for some inputs and thus violates this rule.
